status.en: 120 armed incidents reported in the past seven days, most of them in Abuja, Lagos and Kaduna.
status.nb: 120 væpnede hendelser meldt de siste sju dagene, flest i Abuja, Lagos og Kaduna.

summary.en: Bandits in Zamfara have imposed a N50 million levy on communities and declared no-go zones ahead of the 2027 elections, while gunmen have repeatedly set secondary schools ablaze in Plateau, including a school in Bokkos. In Gombe, Air Force personnel allegedly opened fire on civilians, causing deaths and injuries, and in Benue military forces rescued two abducted women. ISWAP suffered a major loss with a Shura Council member and top commanders killed as troops repelled an attack in Borno. The conflict recorded 1,486 battle-related deaths in 2024, according to UCDP.
summary.nb: Banditter i Zamfara har pålagt lokalsamfunn en avgift på N50 millioner og erklært ingen-go-soner før valget i 2027, mens væpnede menn gjentatte ganger har satt brann på videregående skoler i Plateau, inkludert en skole i Bokkos. I Gombe skal luftforsvarets personell ha åpnet ild mot sivile, noe som har ført til dødsfall og skader, og i Benue reddet militæret to bortførte kvinner. ISWAP led et stort tap da et medlem av Shura-rådet og toppkommandanter ble drept da tropper avverget et angrep i Borno. Konflikten registrerte 1 486 dødsfall i kamp i 2024, ifølge UCDP.

background.title: Boko Haram insurgency
background.extract: The Boko Haram insurgency began in July 2009, when the militant Islamist and jihadist rebel group Boko Haram started an armed rebellion against the government of Nigeria. Boko Haram targets both Muslims and Christians. Attacks are often directed at individuals perceived as supporting the Nigerian government or Islamic State after the split between them, including civil servants, local defense groups, Muslim leaders who oppose the group and other rebels like al-Qaeda and Islamic State. Most attacks are not based on the religion of the victims.
